scenes.title: 1959 Johns Hopkins Optical Bench: The Angled Glass-Slide Edge Unleashing Spikes on the Oscilloscope After Round Light Spots Failed
scenes.era: 1959, Wilmer Institute neurophysiology room, Johns Hopkins Hospital, Baltimore

layout.description: Bright high-key 1959 Johns Hopkins laboratory featuring a white tangent projection screen on the wall, a brass optical slide projector where a **3×1-inch glass slide sticks slightly at a 45-degree diagonal angle** casting a crisp slanted shadow edge across the screen, an articulated matte-white porcelain cat sculpture facing the screen, and a desktop oscilloscope + acoustic speaker cone leaping from flat silence (on round spots) to tall dense spike bursts (on the 45° edge!).

positions.who: David Hubel (mannequin in 1959 rolled-sleeve white dress shirt, slim tie, and lab coat)
positions.where: hand paused on the slightly angled glass slide in the projector slot, eyes wide as the diagonal edge sweeps the white screen and the oscilloscope trace erupts

positions.who: Torsten Wiesel (mannequin in 1959 knit vest under open white lab coat)
positions.where: leaning toward the desktop oscilloscope and speaker monitor pointing at the dramatic spike burst tuned strictly to 45 degrees
positioned calmly facing the white tangent projection screen

props.name: optical slide projector with 45°-angled glass slide & white tangent screen
props.period_detail: contrasts silent round dot stencil against the active diagonal edge of the glass slide itself

props.name: desktop green-trace oscilloscope & '0° Silent | 45° BURST! | 90° Silent' tuning polar chart
props.period_detail: visualizes razor-sharp orientation tuning across clock angles

props.name: articulated matte-white porcelain cat sculpture
props.period_detail: honors R46 porcelain animal rule with clean museum styling

actions.verb_sequence: projects a round spot onto the white screen (oscilloscope trace stays flat) -> slides the glass holder so its 45-degree edge sweeps across the receptive field -> oscilloscope erupts with tall vertical spike bars
rotates the bar to 90 degrees horizontal (trace goes flat again) -> rotates back to 45 degrees (full burst returns!)

reactions.reaction: exchange an electrified grin after five hours of silence suddenly cracked the visual code

scenes.wardrobe: 1959 laboratory attire: rolled-sleeve white cotton shirts, slim dark ties, open white lab coats.
scenes.lighting: Clean high-key laboratory daylight keeping the projection screen and oscilloscope crisp.
scenes.recognition_hook: Five hours of shining round spots produced dead silence — then a stuck glass slide cast one diagonal edge and the neuron roared to life!

key_visual.description: a 1959 lab with two researchers beside an optical projector casting a 45-degree glass-slide edge onto a white screen in front of a porcelain cat sculpture while an oscilloscope jumps with spikes

scenes.title: Why Line Drawings Work & Full Floodlights Fail

layout.description: Sunlit seminar table comparing a blank flooded white board (0 spikes) against a 6-line Picasso-style silhouette sketch (rich V1 edge map).

positions.where: showing how 3 aligned circular LGN centers sum into one Simple-Cell bar detector

props.name: 3-Dot-to-1-Bar Simple Cell wiring plaque & minimal line sketch
props.period_detail: explains both zero response to diffuse light and why humans recognize line art instantly

actions.verb_sequence: aligns three circular '+' centers in a row -> forms one crisp 45° Simple Cell edge filter

reactions.reaction: see instantly how dots build lines and lines build shapes

scenes.recognition_hook: Flood the wall with bright light and V1 yawns — draw five clean black lines and your edge-detector cortex builds an entire face!

scenes.title: Saving Millions of Kids' Vision: Critical-Period Eye Care

layout.description: Warm cheerful sunlit pediatric eye clinic where a smiling toddler wears a colorful pirate-star eye patch over the stronger eye for an hour a day.

positions.where: testing playful 3D stereo picture cards as early patching balances V1 ocular-dominance columns

props.name: cheerful child eye-patch & stereo butterfly card
props.period_detail: direct clinical triumph of Hubel & Wiesel's 1963 critical-period discovery

actions.verb_sequence: reaches out touching the floating 3D stereo wings accurately

scenes.wardrobe: Modern colorful pediatric coat and child sweater.
scenes.recognition_hook: Every child whose eyesight is saved by an early eye-patch or infant cataract surgery owes a thank-you to Hubel & Wiesel's cortical columns.

scenes.title: From 1959 V1 Simple Cells to Modern AI Deep Learning (CNNs)

layout.description: Sunlit workstation displaying Layer-1 convolutional edge filters (0°, 45°, 90°, 135° bars) right beside Hubel & Wiesel's 1959 orientation diagram.

positions.where: comparing biological Simple/Complex cells side-by-side with Convolutional + Pooling network layers

props.name: Layer-1 Gabor edge-filter grid vs 1959 V1 tuning curve
props.period_detail: nearly identical oriented edge detectors in silicon and carbon

actions.verb_sequence: feeds camera frame through Layer 1 -> oriented edges light up just like 1959 V1

reactions.reaction: nods at 65+ years of bio-inspired AI

scenes.recognition_hook: Peer inside Layer 1 of any modern AI vision network and you'll meet the exact 45-degree edge detectors discovered by a jammed slide in 1959.
